욥기-16-1.title: 욥기 16장 1절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-1.exegesis: 35. Bitter irony, illustrating the "unfruitfulness" ( Job 15:34 ) of the wicked. Their conceptions and birthgivings consist solely in mischief, &c. ( Is 33:11 ). prepareth-- hatcheth.

욥기-16-3.exegesis: CHAPTER 16 SECOND SERIES. Job 16:1-22 . Job's Reply. 2. ( Job 13:4 ).

욥기-16-4.title: 욥기 16장 4절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-4.exegesis: 3. "Words of wind," Hebrew. He retorts upon Eliphaz his reproach ( Job 15:2 ). emboldeneth-- literally, "What wearies you so that ye contradict?" that is, What have I said to provoke you? &c. [Schuttens]. Or, as better accords with the first clause, "Wherefore do ye weary yourselves contradicting?" [Umbreit].

욥기-16-5.title: 욥기 16장 5절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-5.exegesis: 4. heap up-- rather, "marshal together (an army of) words against you." shake ... head-- in mockery; it means nodding, rather than shaking; nodding is not with us, as in the East, a gesture of scorn ( Is 37:22 ; Jr 18:16 ; Mt 27:39 ).
욥기-16-5.theologicalNote: 4. heap up-- rather, "marshal together (an army of) words against you." shake ... head-- in mockery; it means nodding, rather than shaking; nodding is not with us, as in the East, a gesture of scorn ( Is 37:22 ; Jr 18:16 ; Mt 27:39 ).

욥기-16-6.title: 욥기 16장 6절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-6.exegesis: 5. strengthen ... with ... mouth-- bitter irony. In allusion to Eliphaz' boasted "consolations" ( Job 15:11 ). Opposed to strengthening with the heart, that is, with real consolation. Translate, "I also (like you) could strengthen with the mouth," that is, with heartless talk: "And the moving of my lips (mere lip comfort) could console (in the same fashion as you do)" [Umbreit]. "Hearty counsel" ( Pr 27:9 ) is the opposite.

욥기-16-7.title: 욥기 16장 7절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-7.exegesis: 6. eased-- literally, "What (portion of my sufferings) goes from me?"
욥기-16-7.theologicalNote: 6. eased-- literally, "What (portion of my sufferings) goes from me?"

욥기-16-8.title: 욥기 16장 8절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-8.exegesis: 7. But now-- rather, "ah!" he-- God. company-- rather, "band of witnesses," namely, those who could attest his innocence (his children, servants, &c.). So the same Hebrew is translated in Job 16:8 . Umbreit makes his "band of witnesses," himself, for, alas! he had no other witness for him. But this is too recondite.

욥기-16-9.title: 욥기 16장 9절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-9.exegesis: 8. filled ... with wrinkles-- Rather (as also the same Hebrew word in Job 22:16 ; English Version, "cut down"), "thou hast fettered me, thy witness" (besides cutting off my "band of witnesses," Job 16:7 ), that is, hast disabled me by pains from properly attesting my innocence. But another "witness" arises against him, namely, his "leanness" or wretched state of body, construed by his friends into a proof of his guilt. The radical meaning of the Hebrew is "to draw together," whence flow the double meaning "to bind" or "fetter," and in Syriac, "to wrinkle." leanness-- meaning also "lie"; implying it was a "false witness."

욥기-16-10.title: 욥기 16장 10절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-10.exegesis: 9. Image from a wild beast. So God is represented ( Job 10:16 ). who hateth me-- rather, "and pursues me hard." Job would not ascribe "hatred" to God ( Psa 50:22 ). mine enemy-- rather, "he sharpens, &c., as an enemy" ( Psa 7:12 ). Darts wrathful glances at me, like a foe ( Job 13:24 ).

욥기-16-11.title: 욥기 16장 11절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-11.exegesis: 10. gaped-- not in order to devour, but to mock him. To fill his cup of misery, the mockery of his friends ( Job 16:10 ) is added to the hostile treatment from God ( Job 16:9 ). smitten ... cheek-- figurative for contemptuous abuse ( La 3:30 ; Mt 5:39 ). gathered themselves-- "conspired unanimously" [Schuttens].

욥기-16-12.title: 욥기 16장 12절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-12.exegesis: 11. the ungodly-- namely, his professed friends, who persecuted him with unkind speeches. turned me over-- literally, "cast me headlong into the hands of the wicked."
욥기-16-12.theologicalNote: 11. the ungodly-- namely, his professed friends, who persecuted him with unkind speeches. turned me over-- literally, "cast me headlong into the hands of the wicked."

욥기-16-13.title: 욥기 16장 13절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-13.exegesis: 12. I was at ease-- in past times ( Job 1:1-3 ). by my neck-- as an animal does its prey (so Job 10:16 ). shaken-- violently; in contrast to his former "ease" ( Psa 102:10 ). Set me up (again). mark-- ( Job 7:20 ; La 3:12 ). God lets me always recover strength, so as to torment me ceaselessly.

욥기-16-14.title: 욥기 16장 14절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-14.exegesis: 13. his archers-- The image of Job 16:12 is continued. God, in making me His "mark," is accompanied by the three friends, whose words wound like sharp arrows. gall-- put for a vital part; so the liver ( La 2:11 ).

욥기-16-15.title: 욥기 16장 15절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-15.exegesis: 14. The image is from storming a fortress by making breaches in the walls ( 2Ki 14:13 ). a giant-- a mighty warrior.
욥기-16-15.theologicalNote: 14. The image is from storming a fortress by making breaches in the walls ( 2Ki 14:13 ). a giant-- a mighty warrior.

욥기-16-16.title: 욥기 16장 16절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-16.exegesis: 15. sewed-- denoting the tight fit of the mourning garment; it was a sack with armholes closely sewed to the body. horn-- image from horned cattle, which when excited tear the earth with their horns. The horn was the emblem of power ( 1Ki 22:11 ). Here, it is in the dust-- which as applied to Job denotes his humiliation from former greatness. To throw one's self in the dust was a sign of mourning; this idea is here joined with that of excited despair, depicted by the fury of a horned beast. The Druses of Lebanon still wear horns as an ornament.

욥기-16-17.title: 욥기 16장 17절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-17.exegesis: 16. foul-- rather, "is red," that is, flushed and heated [Umbreit and Noyes]. shadow of death-- that is, darkening through many tears ( La 5:17 ). Job here refers to Zophar's implied charge ( Job 11:14 ). Nearly the same words occur as to Jesus Christ ( Is 53:9 ). So Job 16:10 above answers to the description of Jesus Christ ( Psa 22:13 ; Is 50:6 , and Job 16:4 to Psa 22:7 ). He alone realized what Job aspired after, namely, outward righteousness of acts and inward purity of devotion. Jesus Christ as the representative man is typified in some degree in every servant of God in the Old Testament.

욥기-16-19.title: 욥기 16장 19절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-19.exegesis: 18. my blood-- that is, my undeserved suffering. He compares himself to one murdered, whose blood the earth refuses to drink up until he is avenged ( Ge 4:10 , 11 ; Eze 24:1 , 8 ; Is 26:21 ). The Arabs say that the dew of heaven will not descend on a spot watered with innocent blood (compare 2Sa 1:21 ). no place-- no resting-place. "May my cry never stop!" May it go abroad! "Earth" in this verse in antithesis to "heaven" ( Job 16:19 ). May my innocence be as well-known to man as it is even now to God!

욥기-16-20.title: 욥기 16장 20절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-20.exegesis: 19. Also now-- Even now, when I am so greatly misunderstood on earth, God in heaven is sensible of my innocence. record-- Hebrew, "in the high places"; Hebrew, "my witness." Amidst all his impatience, Job still trusts in God.

욥기-16-21.title: 욥기 16장 21절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-21.exegesis: 20. Hebrew, "are my scorners"; more forcibly, "my mockers-- my friends!" A heart-cutting paradox [Umbreit]. God alone remains to whom he can look for attestation of his innocence; plaintively with tearful eye, he supplicates for this.

욥기-16-22.title: 욥기 16장 22절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-16-22.exegesis: 21. one-- rather, "He" (God). "Oh, that He would plead for a man (namely, me) against God." Job quaintly says, "God must support me against God; for He makes me to suffer, and He alone knows me to be innocent" [Umbreit]. So God helped Jacob in wrestling against Himself (compare Job 23:6 ; Ge 32:25 ). God in Jesus Christ does plead with God for man ( Ro 8:26 , 27 ). as a man-- literally, "the Son of man." A prefiguring of the advocacy of Jesus Christ--a boon longed for by Job ( Job 9:33 ), though the spiritual pregnancy of his own words, designed for all ages, was but little understood by him ( Psa 80:17 ). for his neighbour-- Hebrew, "friend." Job himself ( Job 42:8 ) pleaded as intercessor for his "friends," though "his scorners" ( Job 16:20 ); so Jesus Christ the Son of man ( Lu 23:34 ); "for friends" ( Joh 15:13-15 ).
